body.statement: For every \(\mathfrak G\in\mathfrak E\), the value \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\) is attained by a globally honest randomized rule and equals the supremum of the Lagrange dual over finite nonnegative atomic coverage measures on the regions \(D_v\) and finite atomic probability measures on \(H_r\). Every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate. An increasing enumeration of finite atomic certificates with rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic support points converges upward to \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), without a bounded-support premise.
body.justification: Attainment and dense atomic duality identify the exact object that the outward primal and dual programs must enclose.
body.gap: Goldenshluger, Juditsky, and Nemirovski establish compact-convex pairwise detector saddles, and Schafer and Stark approximate compact-parameter minimax expected size; neither treats globally honest finite-label rules over an unbounded fan.
body.consumer: CertGluePFL obtains valid lower endpoints without assuming that least-favorable mass is spatially tight.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(m=|\mathcal A|\), let \(\mu\) be Lebesgue measure on \(\mathbb R^d\), and write a randomized rule as \(p=(p_A)_{A\in\mathcal A}\), where each \(p_A\) is a measurable representative, \(p_A\geq0\), and \(\sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1\) almost everywhere.  Denote the set of such vectors by \(\mathscr K\).  This representation is legitimate because \(\mathcal A\) is finite.  We first prove the compactness needed for attainment rather than assume it.

For \(j\geq1\), put \(B_j=[-j,j]^d\), and fix a countable orthonormal basis \((e_{jk})_{k\geq1}\) of \(L^2(B_j)\).  Since \(0\leq p_A\leq1\),
\[
 \|p_A\|_{L^2(B_j)}\leq \mu(B_j)^{1/2}. \tag{1}
\]
Given any sequence in \(\mathscr K\), diagonal extraction over the countable triples \((A,j,k)\) makes every coefficient \(\langle p_A,e_{jk}\rangle_{L^2(B_j)}\) converge.  Bessel's inequality and (1) show that the limiting coefficients define an element \(p_A^{(j)}\in L^2(B_j)\), and the extracted sequence converges weakly to it in \(L^2(B_j)\).  Limits on nested boxes agree because every \(L^2(B_j)\) test function, extended by zero, is an \(L^2(B_{j+1})\) test function.  They therefore define a measurable \(p_A\) on \(\mathbb R^d\).  For every nonnegative \(q\in L^2(B_j)\), weak convergence gives \(\int p_Aq\,d\mu\geq0\).  Taking \(q=(p_A)_{-}\) proves \(p_A\geq0\).  Applying the same argument to \(1-p_A\), and testing \(\sum_Ap_A-1\) and its negative part, proves
\[
 0\leq p_A\leq1,
 \qquad \sum_{A\in\mathcal A}p_A=1
 \quad\text{almost everywhere on every }B_j. \tag{2}
\]
Thus the limit lies in \(\mathscr K\).  The metric obtained by summing the bounded differences of the countably many displayed Fourier coefficients induces the coordinatewise local weak topology on the bounded sets in (1).  The diagonal argument proves sequential compactness in this metric, hence compactness of \(\mathscr K\).

For \(v\in V\), \(h\in D_v\), and \(g\in H_r\), define
\[
 c_{v,h}(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_\Sigma(w-h)
       \sum_{A\ni v}p_A(w)\,dw,
 \qquad
 r_g(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^d}\phi_\Sigma(w-g)
       \sum_A\ell(A)p_A(w)\,dw. \tag{3}
\]
Positive definiteness in \(\text{ass:rational-positive-covariance}\) makes every translated Gaussian density square integrable on each \(B_j\).  Local weak convergence therefore gives convergence of (3) on \(B_j\).  By (2), the absolute contribution off \(B_j\) is at most the corresponding Gaussian tail for \(c_{v,h}\), and at most \(D\) times that tail for \(r_g\).  Letting \(j\to\infty\) proves that every functional in (3) is continuous on \(\mathscr K\).

Consequently
\[
 \mathscr K_\eta=
 \bigcap_{v\in V}\bigcap_{h\in D_v}
 \{p\in\mathscr K:c_{v,h}(p)\geq1-\eta\} \tag{4}
\]
is compact.  It is nonempty because the rule reporting \(V\) surely belongs to it.  The map
\[
 p\longmapsto \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p) \tag{5}
\]
is a supremum of continuous functions and hence is lower semicontinuous.  It attains its minimum on (4).  Gaussian shifts with positive definite covariance are all equivalent to Lebesgue measure, so changing the finitely many coordinates on one common null set turns the minimizer into a measurable Markov kernel valid for every mean.  This proves primal attainment.

We next derive the finite-atomic dual.  Let
\[
 \alpha_v=\sum_{j=1}^{J_v}a_{vj}\delta_{h_{vj}},
 \quad a_{vj}\geq0,quad h_{vj}\in D_v,
 \qquad
 \beta=\sum_{i=1}^{I}b_i\delta_{g_i},
 \quad b_i\geq0,quad \sum_i b_i=1,quad g_i\in H_r. \tag{6}
\]
Define
\[
 a_v(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-h)\,\alpha_v(dh),
 \qquad
 b(w)=\int\phi_\Sigma(w-g)\,\beta(dg). \tag{7}
\]
The Lagrangian associated with the upper-risk epigraph and the coverage inequalities is
\[
 (1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int\sum_{A\subseteq V}p_A(w)
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw. \tag{8}
\]
At each \(w\), (2) ranges over a finite action simplex, so pointwise minimization of (8) is attained at a vertex.  Measurability follows by choosing the first minimizing action in a fixed enumeration.  Hence the dual value is exactly
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 =(1-\eta)\sum_v\alpha_v(D_v)
 +\int_{\mathbb R^d}\min_{A\subseteq V}
 \left\{b(w)\ell(A)-\sum_{v\in A}a_v(w)\right\}dw. \tag{9}
\]
For every \(p\in\mathscr K_\eta\), equations (3), (6), and (8) give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)
 &\leq \sum_i b_i r_{g_i}(p)
   +\sum_{v,j}a_{vj}\{(1-\eta)-c_{v,h_{vj}}(p)\}\\
 &\leq \sup_{g\in H_r}r_g(p).
 \end{aligned} \tag{10}
\]
Thus every finite atomic dual is a valid lower certificate.

It remains to prove that these certificates are exhaustive.  Fix \(t<M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\).  The sets
\[
 \{p:r_g(p)>t\},\quad g\in H_r,
 \qquad
 \{p:c_{v,h}(p)<1-\eta\},\quad v\in V, h\in D_v, \tag{11}
\]
form an open cover of \(\mathscr K\): an honest rule has supremum risk at least \(M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)>t\), whereas a nonhonest rule violates one inequality in (4).  Compactness gives a finite subcover with risk points \(g_1,\ldots,g_I\) and coverage points \((v_j,h_j)\), \(j=1,\ldots,J\).  The compact convex set
\[
 Y=\left\{
 \bigl((r_{g_i}(p)-t)_{i\leq I},
 ((1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p))_{j\leq J}\bigr):p\in\mathscr K
 \right\} \tag{12}
\]
is disjoint from the closed negative orthant \(\mathbb R_-^{I+J}\).  To see the sign and strictness of a separator directly, minimize the squared distance between (12) and the negative orthant.  Projection onto that orthant and the two first-order variational inequalities yield a separating normal with nonnegative coordinates.  Disjointness and compactness make the distance positive.  Therefore there are \(\gamma_i,\zeta_j\geq0\), not all zero, and \(q>0\) such that
\[
 \sum_i\gamma_i\{r_{g_i}(p)-t\}
 +\sum_j\zeta_j\{(1-\eta)-c_{v_j,h_j}(p)\}
 \geq q
 \quad\text{for every }p\in\mathscr K. \tag{13}
\]
For the rule reporting \(V\), every coverage deficit in (13) equals \(-\eta\).  Hence \(G=\sum_i\gamma_i>0\).  Set \(b_i=\gamma_i/G\) and give the coverage atom \((v_j,h_j)\) mass \(a_j=\zeta_j/G\).  Dividing (13) by \(G\) and taking the infimum over \(p\in\mathscr K\) shows, by (9),
\[
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta)\geq t+q/G>t. \tag{14}
\]
Combining (10) and (14), then letting \(t\uparrow M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)\), proves
\[
 M_{\mathfrak G,\eta}(r)
 =\sup_{\alpha,\beta\ {
m finite\ atomic}}
 \mathcal D(\alpha,\beta). \tag{15}
\]

Finally we prove the asserted effective dense support restriction.  Every \(D_v\) is a finite union of rational polyhedra.  The conditions defining \(H_r\) consist of membership and nonmembership in finitely many such unions and inequalities of the form
\[
 \inf_{x:A x\leq b}(h-x)'\Sigma^{-1}(h-x)\geq r^2. \tag{16}
\]
Introducing the closest-point variable in (16) and eliminating it produces a semialgebraic formula over \(\mathbb Q\); equivalently, one may enumerate the finitely many active sets of the strictly convex quadratic program.  Thus \(D_v\) and \(H_r\) are rational semialgebraic sets.  Enumerate rational open boxes.  Exact sign decomposition of the finitely many defining polynomials decides whether such a box meets the set and, when it does, recursively isolates a real-algebraic sample point: in one variable this is rational root isolation, and in dimension \(k\) one isolates the finitely many real roots in the last coordinate over each sign cell already isolated in dimension \(k-1\).  Every relative neighborhood contains a rational box meeting the set, so the resulting real-algebraic points are dense in each \(D_v\) and in \(H_r\), including zero-dimensional components.

If \(x_n\to x\), then \(\phi_\Sigma(\cdot-x_n)\to\phi_\Sigma(\cdot-x)\) pointwise.  Moreover
\[
 \int|\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n)-\phi_\Sigma(w-x)|\,dw
 =2-2\int\min\{\phi_\Sigma(w-x_n),\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\}\,dw\longrightarrow0, \tag{17}
\]
because the minimum is dominated by \(\phi_\Sigma(w-x)\).  Hence perturbing finitely many support points to the enumerated algebraic points and perturbing their weights to nonnegative rationals, preserving \(\sum_i b_i=1\), makes the mixtures in (7) converge in \(L^1\).  The elementary inequality
\[
 \left|\min_A x_A-\min_A y_A\right|
 \leq\max_A|x_A-y_A| \tag{18}
\]
then shows from (9) that the dual values converge.  Thus rational weights and rationally encoded real-algebraic supports are dense among all finite atomic certificates.

For completeness, the value of each such certificate is a computable real.  On a rational box, every Gaussian mixture in (7) has computable uniform derivative bounds, so lower and upper Riemann sums for the finite minimum in (9) converge effectively.  Outside the box its absolute value is bounded by \(D b(w)+\sum_va_v(w)\), whose finitely many Gaussian tails have effective outward rational bounds.  Dovetail the support-and-weight enumeration with these two-sided integral enclosures.  Maintain a current certificate and replace it only when the certified lower enclosure of a new candidate exceeds the certified upper enclosure of the current one.  Its exact dual values are nondecreasing.  If its limit were smaller than (15), a candidate separated from that limit by a positive amount would eventually be recognized and would force a replacement.  Therefore the resulting increasing sequence converges upward to (15).  No spatial truncation of the permissible dual support was used.
